slides.title: Welcome to HTML Media Elements
slides.content: # HTML Media Elements 🎬 Rich media—images, vector illustrations, audio, video, and interactive frames—bring web pages to life. ## What you'll master: - 🖼️ **The `` Element** - Essential attributes, dimensions, and layout shift prevention - 📱 **Responsive Images** - `srcset`, `sizes`, and the `` element - ⚡ **Next-Gen Formats & Lazy Loading** - WebP, AVIF, and `loading="lazy"` - 🎵 **Native Audio & Video** - Multi-source embeds, controls, and accessibility tracks - 🪟 **iFrames & Security** - Embedding external content safely with `sandbox`

slides.title: The Element Fundamentals
slides.content: # The `` Element Fundamentals 🖼️ The `` element embeds an image into an HTML page. It is a void (self-closing) element. ```html_not ``` ## Mandatory Attributes: 1. **`src`** (Source): Path or URL to the image file. 2. **`alt`** (Alternative Text): Text description displayed if image fails to load, and read aloud by screen readers. 3. **`width` & `height`**: Defining aspect ratio prevents Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)!

slides.title: The Power of the alt Attribute
slides.content: # Writing Perfect `alt` Text ♿ The `alt` attribute is the single most important accessibility feature for web images. ## Rules for Writing Alt Text: - ✅ **Be descriptive & concise:** Describe the contents and context of the image. - ❌ **Don't say "Image of..." or "Picture of...":** Screen readers already announce that it's an image. - 🎯 **Decorative Images:** If an image is purely decorative (like a background flourish or divider), use an empty `alt=""` so screen readers ignore it! ```html_not ```

slides.title: Preventing Layout Shift (CLS)
slides.content: # Preventing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) ⚡ Before HTML loads an image, it doesn't know its dimensions, causing the page layout to jerk and jump as images finish downloading. ## The Modern Solution: Always provide explicit `width` and `height` attributes on ``: ```html_not ``` ```css_not .responsive-img { width: 100%; height: auto; /* Preserves aspect ratio automatically! */ } ``` Modern browsers calculate the aspect ratio from the attributes before the image downloads, reserving exact placeholder space on screen!

slides.title: Responsive Images with srcset
slides.content: # Responsive Images with `srcset` 📱 Serving a 4K desktop image to a small mobile smartphone wastes user data and slows down loading times. `srcset` solves this! ```html_not ``` ## How It Works: - `srcset`: Lists available image files along with their natural pixel width in `w` units. - `sizes`: Informs the browser how wide the image will be displayed at different viewport media queries. - The browser automatically chooses the optimal image size to download!

slides.title: The <picture> Element & Art Direction
slides.content: # The `` Element & Art Direction 🎨 When you want to serve completely different images based on screen size (Art Direction), or modern file formats, use ``. ```html_not ```

slides.title: Serving Modern Image Formats (WebP & AVIF)
slides.content: # Modern Formats: WebP & AVIF 🚀 Next-generation formats like **WebP** and **AVIF** achieve 30% to 50% smaller file sizes than legacy JPEGs/PNGs at identical visual quality. ```html_not ``` Browsers evaluate `` tags from top to bottom, picking the first supported format!

slides.title: Native Lazy Loading
slides.content: # Native Lazy Loading with `loading='lazy'` ⚡ Native lazy loading delays loading offscreen images and iframes until the user scrolls near them, speeding up initial page render dramatically! ```html_not ``` > ⚠️ **Hero Image Warning:** Never put `loading="lazy"` on your top hero image! That hurts your Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) performance score.

slides.title: Native Video Embedding (<video>)
slides.content:
# Native Video Embedding (`<video>`) 🎬

HTML5 `<video>` embeds video files without plugins:

```html_not
<video controls width="640" height="360" poster="thumb.jpg" preload="metadata">
  <source src="intro.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <source src="intro.webm" type="video/webm">
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>
```

## Attribute Breakdown:
- `controls`: Displays default browser playback controls.
- `poster`: Image shown before play is pressed.
- `autoplay`: Starts automatically (must usually be combined with `muted` to work).
- `loop`: Restarts playback upon finishing.
- `playsinline`: Prevents automatic full-screen expansion on iOS Safari.

slides.title: Background Video Autoplay
Timed Text & Subtitles with <track>
slides.content:
# Timed Text & Subtitles with `<track>` 💬

The `<track>` tag adds subtitles, captions, or descriptions using WebVTT (`.vtt`) format:

```html_not
<video controls width="640" height="360">
  <source src="presentation.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  
  <track src="subs_en.vtt" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" label="English" default>
  <track src="subs_es.vtt" kind="subtitles" srclang="es" label="Spanish">
</video>
```

## Kinds of Tracks:
- `subtitles`: Translations for dialogue.
- `captions`: Dialogue plus sound effects (e.g. `[Thunder rumbles]`) for hearing impaired users.
- `descriptions`: Text description of visual video events for screen readers.

slides.title: Native Audio Embedding (<audio>)
slides.content:
# Native Audio Embedding (`<audio>`) 🎵

Embed podcasts, voice recordings, or sound effects:

```html_not
<audio controls>
  <source src="sound.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
  <source src="sound.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
  Your browser does not support audio playback.
</audio>
```

Supported formats: MP3 (universal), AAC, WAV, OGG.

slides.title: Embedding External Content with <iframe>
slides.content:
# Embedding Content with `<iframe>` 🪟

An Inline Frame (`<iframe>`) embeds an external webpage, YouTube video, or Google Map directly into your page:

```html_not
<iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ"
        title="YouTube video player"
        width="560"
        height="315"
        style="border:0;"
        allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture"
        allowfullscreen>
</iframe>
```

> ♿ **Accessibility Requirement:** Every `<iframe>` **must** have a descriptive `title` attribute so screen reader users understand what the frame contains!

slides.title: iFrame Security with sandbox
slides.content:
# iFrame Security: The `sandbox` Attribute 🔒

Embedding untrusted third-party content creates security vulnerabilities. The `sandbox` attribute restricts the embedded page's permissions!

```html_not
<!-- Maximum security: blocks scripts, forms, popups, and same-origin cookies -->
<iframe src="untrusted.html" sandbox title="User submission preview"></iframe>

<!-- Selective permissions -->
<iframe src="widget.html"
        sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms"
        title="Third-party widget">
</iframe>
```

Without permissions, a sandboxed iframe cannot execute JavaScript or submit forms!

slides.title: Performance Optimization for Media
slides.content:
# Media Performance Optimization Checklist ⚡

Follow this production checklist for blazing fast media:
1. **Compress all images:** Run through tools like Squoosh or ImageOptim before deployment.
2. **Serve AVIF/WebP:** Deliver modern formats with `<picture>`.
3. **Always specify dimensions:** Set `width` and `height` to prevent layout shift.
4. **Enable `loading="lazy"`:** On all offscreen images.
5. **Use responsive `srcset`:** Match device resolution (1x, 2x Retina).
6. **Mute background videos:** Ensure autoplay succeeds with `muted playsinline`.

slides.title: Summary & Next Steps
slides.content:
# Media Elements Mastered! 🌟

You are now an expert in embedding high-performance, accessible media on the web!

## Key Takeaways:
- ✅ **Images:** Use `src`, descriptive `alt`, and `width`/`height` to eliminate layout shift.
- ✅ **Responsive Images:** Use `srcset` and `sizes` for resolution switching.
- ✅ **Art Direction:** Use `<picture>` for cropping and modern format fallbacks (AVIF/WebP).
- ✅ **Native Video & Audio:** `<video>` and `<audio>` with `<source>` and `<track>`.
- ✅ **iFrame Security:** Always add a `title` and lock down with `sandbox`.
